contribution_types.label: General
contribution_types.scope: The default contribution type for submissions that fit no other category.
contribution_types.quote: General: Most submissions will fall into this category.

contribution_types.label: Theory
contribution_types.scope: Contribution consisting primarily of theoretical analyses and proofs.
contribution_types.quote: Theory: The main contribution is via theoretical analyses and proofs.

contribution_types.label: Use-Inspired
contribution_types.scope: Contribution framed or designed to meet the needs of a specific real-world application.
contribution_types.quote: Use-Inspired: The main contribution is in framing or designing approaches to meet the needs of a specific real-world application.

contribution_types.label: Concept & Feasibility
contribution_types.scope: A highly novel, high-reward idea whose scope exceeds what one paper can validate.
contribution_types.quote: Concept & Feasibility: The main contribution is a highly novel, high potential reward idea with scope beyond what can be validated in a single paper.

contribution_types.label: Negative Results
contribution_types.scope: Contribution whose value lies in understanding a negative result.
contribution_types.quote: Negative Results: The main contribution is in understanding a negative result.

review_criteria.name: Quality
review_criteria.official_explanation: Technical soundness and support for the claims, including appropriateness of methods.
review_criteria.quote: Is the submission technically sound? Are claims well supported (e.g., by theoretical analysis or experimental results)? Are the methods used appropriate?

review_criteria.name: Originality
review_criteria.official_explanation: New insights, deepened understanding, or important properties of existing methods; novelty of method is not required.
review_criteria.quote: Does the work provide new insights, deepen understanding, or highlight important properties of existing methods?

review_criteria.name: Significance
review_criteria.official_explanation: Impact and likely reuse by researchers or practitioners, and demonstrable advance over prior work.
review_criteria.quote: Are the results impactful for the community? Are others (researchers or practitioners) likely to use the ideas or build on them?

review_criteria.name: Clarity
review_criteria.official_explanation: Clear writing and organization, and enough information for an expert to reproduce results.
review_criteria.quote: Is the submission clearly written? Is it well organized? Does it adequately inform the reader?

review_criteria.name: Contribution Type Fit
review_criteria.official_explanation: The review is interpreted against the contribution type the authors selected.
review_criteria.quote: Reviewers should assess a submission according to the Contribution Type selected by the authors.

review_criteria.name: Reproducibility
review_criteria.official_explanation: Submissions should carry enough information to reproduce the reported results.
review_criteria.quote: The paper checklist is intended to help authors reflect on a wide variety of issues relating to responsible machine learning research, including reproducibility, transparency, research ethics, and societal impact.

review_criteria.name: Submission Compliance
review_criteria.official_explanation: Track selection matters: irrelevant or duplicate submissions risk desk rejection from every track.
review_criteria.quote: Irrelevant or duplicate papers risk desk rejection from all tracks.

mandatory_policy.statement: The main text of a submission may not exceed nine content pages, including all figures and tables.
mandatory_policy.quote: The main text of a submitted paper is limited to nine content pages, including all figures and tables.

mandatory_policy.statement: Submissions, including supplementary and linked material, must be anonymized and free of identifying information.
mandatory_policy.quote: All submissions must be anonymized and may not contain any identifying information that may violate the double-blind reviewing policy.

mandatory_policy.statement: Authors must complete the NeurIPS paper checklist included in the paper template.
mandatory_policy.quote: authors are required to complete the paper checklist included in the paper template.

mandatory_policy.statement: Submitting the same work to NeurIPS and later to another archival venue while under NeurIPS review is prohibited.
mandatory_policy.quote: In addition, we explicitly prohibit submitting work to NeurIPS and then later submitting the same work to another archival venue while it is still under review at NeurIPS.

mandatory_policy.statement: Agents and LLMs cannot be listed as authors; authors remain responsible for all content.
mandatory_policy.quote: agents and LLMs cannot be authors

recommended_practice.statement: Important, original or non-standard use of agents/LLMs in implementing the method should be described in the experimental setup.
recommended_practice.quote: The use of agents and/or LLMs in implementing the method should be described in the experimental setup section (or equivalent) if it is an important, original, or non-standard component of the approach

recommended_practice.statement: Authors are encouraged to upload code as supplementary material to help reviewers assess quality.
recommended_practice.quote: We encourage authors to upload their code specifically as part of their supplementary material in order to help reviewers assess the quality of the work.

recommended_practice.statement: Authors are encouraged to follow dataset best practices such as persistent identifiers and metadata standards.
recommended_practice.quote: You are also encouraged to conform to the following best practices

compliance_checks.requirement: Main text is at most nine content pages including figures and tables.
Submission uses the mandatory NeurIPS LaTeX style file; no Word template is accepted.
No author-identifying information anywhere in the PDF or supplementary material.
Completed NeurIPS paper checklist is included in the submitted PDF.
Every author has an OpenReview profile by the abstract deadline.
No overlapping archival submission is under review elsewhere.

changes_from_prior_year.change: NeurIPS 2026 reviewer guidance is organized by Contribution Type (General, Theory, Use-Inspired, Concept & Feasibility, Negative Results); the 2025 Reviewer Guidelines publish no such taxonomy.
NeurIPS 2026 adds responsible reviewing/ACing safeguards, including possible desk rejection of grossly negligent reviewer-authors and AC-authors.
Whether the 2025 camera-ready funding-disclosure requirement still applies in 2026 is not stated by any captured 2026 source.

unknown_policies.question: Must NeurIPS 2026 camera-ready papers include a funding disclosure?
unknown_policies.reason: The 2025 CFP required it, but no captured 2026 source states it; a prior-year rule is never inherited.

unknown_policies.question: What is the full text of the NeurIPS 2026 policy on LLM use that the 2026 sources reference?
unknown_policies.reason: The dedicated LLM policy page was not captured; only the Main Track Handbook statements are quoted here.
